extracted.intended_audience: content marketers and PR professionals (in-house marketers, comms teams, PR for content-driven campaigns)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for using research- and content-first press releases to earn coverage, backlinks, and long-tail SEO, including what to include in the release, distribution tactics, measurement metrics, and anti-patterns to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-first PR strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Position PR as an extension of content marketing: create publishable content first, then use PR to amplify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owned media is the foundation; press releases are used primarily for amplification and driving earned coverage rather than announcing product/company vanity news.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owned media as the foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize publishing substantive content on channels you control before pitching it to the press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use blogs, resource hubs, and proprietary reports as the canonical source so earned links and coverage point back to owned assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press releases serve content amplification
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases to amplify existing content (research/data/guides) rather than as standalone promotional announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing: lead with data and findings; the release's role is to earn backlinks and coverage that benefits owned content and SEO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail SEO through earned coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for earned coverage that contributes to long-term organic search visibility and cumulative SEO benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure long-tail search improvements over time (e.g., 90 days) and prioritize coverage that links back to owned content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repurposing content across channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Take the same research/content and adapt it for multiple channels to maximize reach and reinforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: publish the primary report on owned site, create LinkedIn carousels, pitch podcasts, make infographics for social and press use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create substantive content (research, data, guides)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with high-quality, substantive assets—original research, data, or comprehensive guides—that are inherently newsworthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should be robust enough to justify outreach and to be cited by journalists and bloggers (surprising findings increase pickup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch the content angle to journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Craft and send pitches that highlight the newsworthy angle of your content to journalists who cover the topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeted pitching (reporter beats) is preferred over mass blasts; emphasize the most newsworthy data point or trend in the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earn coverage with backlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: The PR objective is to earn mentions and backlinks from journalists and bloggers that reference your owned content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backlinks provide SEO value and help long-tail rankings; prioritize outlets and writers likely to link rather than only mention.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEO compounds over time
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that SEO benefits from earned coverage accumulate gradually rather than immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track organic performance over months (not just days) to see the cumulative impact of coverage and backlinks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inbound leads grow
rubrics_metrics.description: One ultimate success metric is observable increase in inbound leads attributable to the earned coverage and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie coverage and organic traffic to pipeline metrics to demonstrate business impact rather than focusing solely on vanity metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research with surprising findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use proprietary research that uncovers unexpected or noteworthy findings to attract press interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surprising or counterintuitive results are more likely to be picked up and linked to by reporters and bloggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry benchmark reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish benchmark studies that provide comparative industry data useful to journalists and readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmarks are frequently cited and evergreen; ensure methodology is clear to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Year-over-year trend analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce analyses that demonstrate change over time, highlighting trends or shifts in the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trends help journalists tell stories; include clear visuals and explicit comparisons to prior periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive how-to guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Create in-depth practical guides that serve as authoritative resources and can be referenced by media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How-to content should be actionable and well-structured to earn links and social shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools and calculators with proprietary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop interactive tools or calculators built on proprietary data to drive utility and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tools increase engagement and are strong link magnets; ensure data sources are documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: data finding, not company news
rubrics_metrics.description: Write headlines that highlight a data point or finding rather than phrasing the headline as company news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists respond to topical, data-first headlines; avoid promotional/company-centric wording in the headline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lede: 5 W's about the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Open releases with the who/what/when/where/why of the data to quickly communicate news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the key finding clear in the first paragraph so journalists can immediately assess the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: methodology + key findings + implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Include clear methodology, the main findings, and their practical or industry implications in the release body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document methodology to increase credibility and to make it easier for journalists to report accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quote: from research lead
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an authoritative quote from the person who led the research or the most relevant expert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should contextualize findings and suggest implications or next steps; make the speaker available for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia: charts, infographics
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide visual assets (charts, infographics) to make findings easier to consume and to increase pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality visuals increase the chance of reuse and linking; include image files and embed codes when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution: trade press + bloggers + LinkedIn
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute releases to a mix of trade press, relevant bloggers, and social channels like LinkedIn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a diversified approach—targeted journalist outreach plus blogger outreach and owned/social promotion for compounding reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch to journalists who cover the topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and reach out to journalists with demonstrated coverage of the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match angle to reporter beat; personalization and relevance outperform mass outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bloggers in the space (long-tail SEO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include niche bloggers in outreach to capture long-tail SEO opportunities and targeted audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Smaller sites often link and provide durable SEO value; prioritize those likely to contextualize the data for their readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry newsletters
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch industry newsletters as a distribution channel to reach engaged niche audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsletters can drive referral traffic and often syndicate or link to original reporting—good for both awareness and links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire for SEO floor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use wire distribution services to establish a baseline of discoverability and an SEO floor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services can provide broad dissemination but should not be the sole tactic; wire-only distribution is listed as weak when used alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: LinkedIn carousels
rubrics_metrics.description: Repurpose findings into LinkedIn carousel posts to reach a professional audience and generate social engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual, bite-sized summaries perform well and can drive traffic back to the full report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast pitch (research as discussion topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch the research as a guest discussion topic on relevant podcasts to extend reach and authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Podcasts can provide deeper storytelling opportunities and introduce data to engaged audiences who may link or share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earned backlinks (SEO value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count and value backlinks earned from coverage as a primary SEO-oriented metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Backlinks should be tracked for quality and relevance; they are a leading indicator of long-term organic growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure social engagement and shares as an indicator of resonance and reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social shares are useful for amplification but should be tied back to traffic and downstream business impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand mentions (with and without links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track mentions of the brand across media, both linked and unlinked, as signals of awareness and reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlinked mentions may still provide value; prioritize converting mentions into links where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pipeline impact attributable
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute measurable pipeline or lead-generation impact back to earned coverage and content-driven PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tracking, UTM parameters, and attribution models to show business value rather than only PR metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-tail search rankings (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track improvements in long-tail organic search rankings over a 90-day window as a key success measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrow-window ranking changes can be noisy—evaluate longer-term trend changes to assess campaign effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotional press releases without data (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid press releases that are purely promotional and lack substantive data or news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such releases tend not to earn meaningful coverage or links; they perform poorly for SEO and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic 'leading provider' framing (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely on vague claims like 'leading provider' as the core framing of a release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists ignore puffery; focus on verifiable, newsworthy data points instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content with no methodology (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid publishing findings without documenting the methodology behind them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of methodology undermines credibility and reduces chances of pickup; always include or link to methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-only distribution (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying solely on wire services without targeted outreach is ineffective for content-driven PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire can be part of the mix for baseline visibility but should be complemented by targeted pitching to reporters and bloggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-blast outreach (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mass-blast outreach to large lists without tailoring; it reduces effectiveness and harms relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personalized, beat-appropriate outreach yields higher pickup and more meaningful coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (CoSchedule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise checklist summarizing CoSchedule's quality standards for content-driven releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Items: Content-first strategy; Original data in release; Methodology documented; Charts/infographics included; Distribution to bloggers + journalists; Long-tail SEO measurement. Use this checklist to evaluate whether a release is likely to earn coverage and SEO value.
